tiers.v1: Addressable preset category. At least one schema-valid preset with a deterministic golden render is required before the type counts as shipped.
tiers.later: Recorded. Not a v1 preset category.
tiers.out: Out of scope. Not a preset category.

poseNotes.contact: The front heel meets the ground and the back heel is about to lift. The stride is the distance between the feet.
poseNotes.down: The front foot is planted and the knee bends under the weight. The body is lowest.
poseNotes.passing: The support leg is nearly straight under the body. The free leg passes with a bent knee. The legs cross.
poseNotes.up: The support leg pushes to the toe. The body is highest, just before the next contact.

notes.walk: Four-beat. Two or three feet stay on the ground. A hind foot replaces the front foot on the same side.
notes.amble: Faster than the walk, with a shorter contact.
notes.trot: Two-beat diagonal. The body lifts slightly between contacts.
notes.canter: Three-beat, with a left or right lead. Later tier.
notes.gallop: Four-beat plus a suspension, with chest and hip offset. Later tier.

locomotion.bird: Downstroke makes lift and thrust. Upstroke folds and reduces area. Do not draw flight as swimming through air.
locomotion.fish: A sine wave that grows from the head to the tail.
locomotion.snake: A lateral wave. Six to twelve segments.

methods.cutout: v1 standard. Parent-child groups and pivot rotation. The same keys survive a part swap. No bone hierarchy.
methods.frameSwap: Later. Needs a symbol visibility track. A tempo change increases the drawn set.
methods.pathMorph: Later. Interpolation requires the same command count, kinds, and order.

antiFootSlide.example: At 24 fps, a 24-frame cycle is 1 second. An 80 px stride has a 0.5 second step and a ground speed of 160 px per second.
antiFootSlide.plantedFoot: A planted foot stays fixed in world space until the heel lifts. Root travel over one step equals the stride.

engineGaps.summary: Cycle metadata and loop-safe keys: stridePx, cycleMs, contact flags.
Seeded randomness and a particle emitter. v1 uses a fixed instance count.
